newsitem.title: HAITI: U.N. police trainer wounded in Haiti slum attack.
newsitem.headline: U.N. police trainer wounded in Haiti slum attack.

text.p: Armed gangsters attacked two Algerian U.N. civilian police trainers who were patrolling a Port-au-Prince slum on Saturday, shooting and wounding one of the officers.

"We were stopped because a bus had broken down and several guys with guns came on the right and on the left," said U.N. civilian police officer Maizi Mohamed, who was recovering from a gunshot wound in a U.N. hospital.
"One shot into the car, breaking the window. When I pulled out my gun to defend myself the guy shot me in the arm."
Mohamed said he fired one shot at the attacker before driving away. Another Algerian trainer on the passenger side ducked when the shots were fired and was unharmed.

Cite Soleil, a sprawling slum of some 200,000 of Haiti's poorest people, has been terrorised by gang violence which left as many as 11 people dead last month. U.N. civilian police trainers have been helping the Haitian National Police to secure the area.
The violence continued on Sunday, when gunshots were exchanged between several Haitian National Police and armed gangsters who fired on them from a motorcycle.
The U.N. police trainers and Haitian police said they believed many of the gangs were involved in drug trafficking, leading to gang wars and attacks on police officers.
Saturday's attack on the trainers was the first aggression against the U.N. forces in the slum.

The civilian police trainers supplement a U.N. military peacekeeping force which replaced some 20,000 U.S. troops who restored former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power after a 1991 military coup.

Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy announced last week that Canadian troops would stay until the end of the year. The official U.N. mandate ends on July 31, but due to a crime wave that has left as many as 40 dead in recent weeks, Canadian officials have said the mission would remain.
